propositions: Cancelled ACLI link deletes (stderr: command cancelled) are counted as applied links via an except arm with no idempotent marker check, inflating links_applied and hiding failures from the silent-noop canary.
The root cause is missing --yes flag on both acli link subcommands; without it, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL reads EOF at the confirmation prompt and ACLI exits non-zero deterministically every pass.

The except subprocess.CalledProcessError arm in _update_one_dispatch_links increments _links_applied without printing, so no update_one: failed lines appear and the failure is invisible except in the raw ACLI stderr output.

A cancelled delete must count toward links_failed (new counter) and not links_applied; genuine idempotent races (404/409/does-not-exist/not-found on either stderr or stdout) must still count as applied.
Both link dispatch and link removal logic must be extracted to separate functions to avoid C901 complexity ceiling violation.
The batch_outcome logging must print links_failed=<n> to surface the new counter and allow the silent-noop canary to detect non-idempotent failures.
